$comment: This repo's adherence record against the shared knowledge library. FOUR states, not two. `rules` = ADOPTED (a local gate enforces it, baseline measured here). `satisfied` = the principle applies and this repo already meets it, by a named mechanism, with a command that reproduces the measurement. `declined` = reviewed and rejected for this repo, with a reason. Anything in library-index.json in none of these is UNREVIEWED — reported, never failed on. The `satisfied` state exists because the first two adoptions attempted here BOTH measured 0 true positives: writing a gate from a principle without reading the code first produces ~0% precision, and the honest output was 'already fine, by a better mechanism' rather than a new rule.

satisfied.mechanism: Three correct patterns, none of which is the library's. (1) features/schranka/followCodec.ts:25 puts the SCHEMA VERSION IN THE KEY (politicas:schranka:v1), so a shape change becomes a new key and stale data is never found — no migration code can be wrong because none exists. (2) features/graph/GraphPage.tsx:41,55 validates on read: an isVariant() type guard checks the stored string against the current VARIANTS list and falls back to 'mapa'. (3) features/landing/referendum/ReferendumPage.tsx:95 tests EXISTENCE only and never parses the value, so there is no shape to drift; it is try/caught for private mode and degrades open.
satisfied.evidence: Measured 2026-08-14: exactly 3 getItem sites repo-wide, and ZERO sites that JSON.parse storage outside the accessor. A gate written against this principle before reading the code matched all 5 code occurrences and scored 0 true positives — it would have had someone add version keys to two files that do not need them, and possibly break the existence-only check.
satisfied.upstream: Version-in-the-key has been sent back to the library: the principle currently only WARNS that a stored shape can drift from the code reading it, which crashes exactly the users holding old data and never the developer whose storage is already current.

satisfied.mechanism: This is a RESULT-RETURNING codebase, and that is a different — arguably stronger — answer than the library's. The library's clause is 'every caught error must reach a reporting door' (Sentry, toast, log), which is calibrated to a codebase where an error is a side effect. Here an error becomes part of the RETURN TYPE: features/money/reviewActions.ts:126 returns {status:'error', message}, lib/analysis/verdict.ts:305 returns {ok:false, errors:[...]}, lib/ingest/sources/kiosek.ts:203 stores lastErr and rethrows after the retry loop. A caller cannot ignore a Result the way it can ignore an unreported side effect, and a type checker enforces it where a lint rule only counts.
satisfied.evidence: Measured 2026-08-14: 106 catch clauses in product roots, of which 5 have no console/log/report/throw inside the catch body. All 5 were opened and read; all 5 return or rethrow the error. Second gate attempted here, second 0/3 precision result on the sampled sites.
satisfied.verifiedBy: grep -rEn "catch\s*\(" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx app components features lib | grep -v '.test.' | wc -l
satisfied.caveat: SATISFIED IS A SNAPSHOT, NOT A GUARANTEE. Nothing here gates a regression — this repo's own custom/no-silent-catch and custom/no-silent-null-catch cover the empty-catch and null-return shapes at "error", but neither sees a Result-returning catch that drops the error on the floor. Re-run verifiedBy before trusting this entry.

declined.reason: No Tauri IPC surface exists here — verified zero .rs files and no src-tauri directory. There is no command boundary to authorize.

Describes adding a #[tauri::command] and regenerating ts-rs bindings. This repo has no Rust and no IPC layer; its equivalent boundary is Next.js route handlers, which is a different situation the library has not yet written.
Concerns the flat global namespace of Tauri command wire keys. Next.js routes are namespaced by the filesystem, so the situation this principle exists to solve cannot arise here.
Specific to ts-rs generating TypeScript from Rust structs. There is no generated cross-language type boundary in this repo; types are authored once in TypeScript.
No Rust to test. This repo's equivalent lane is Vitest plus its own eslint-plugin rule tests, both already wired into npm run check.
Concerns cargo feature unification and per-feature compilation. There is no cargo build here; the analogous axis would be Next.js build-time env, which the library has not written as a principle.

Describes rusqlite row-to-Rust-struct mapping by column index and name. No rusqlite, no Rust structs. The general clause about positional mapping being fragile may still apply if this repo adds a SQL layer, so re-open this if scripts/gen-migration.ts grows into one.
